_note: CARGO RUN, INDUSTRIAL, letter b: MB41a's shape exactly (talk, pickup, talk on another planet; the hand-back takes the cargo). The two ends know each other and the player is the only thing travelling between them.
WHY IT MATTERS VARIES from the toolbox's mentor-to-apprentice: LUCK: a worn-out drill bit lent to a sister crew on a dry stretch; the foreman will not ask after her old crew and sends it anyway.
Sites: industrial OE themes (manual 32: Mining 7 POI types, Power 8, UnderConstruction 8 in vanilla). The pools are small; the lint's pool count decides whether they deal often enough.
Own people, voices, opener and close, not 41a's (card 20261031-071709). Voices borrowed until his ear casts them. No names or places in any voiced line.

prose.name: Hauling: Lucky Drill Bit to <SecondPlanet>
prose.briefing: A mining foreman at the <Place> is lending her crew's lucky drill bit to the crew at the <SecondPlace>, who haven't struck anything worth hauling in weeks.
prose.card: Delivery Contract. Deliver a drill bit from the <Place>, <Planet> to the <SecondPlace>, <SecondPlanet>. Payment on delivery.

beats.objective: Talk to the mining foreman at the <Place>
beats.journal: The foreman is lending her crew's lucky drill bit to the crew she came up with, who have hit nothing in weeks. I need to collect it and take it to them.

person.name: Dora Quayle
hellos: Hard hats on past this point. Ideally.

greeting: You're the hauler? Good. The bit's just there, worn flat and useless for drilling, and it's the luckiest thing on this rock. The crew I came up with hasn't hit a seam in weeks. They're too proud to ask, so I'm just sending it.

exchanges.prompt: I'll take the bit to them.
reply: Mind it. I want it back when they've had a good month, and you can tell them I said so.

exchanges.prompt: Weeks without a seam is usually the rock, not the luck.
reply: It's always the rock. You try telling a crew that at the bottom of a dry shaft.
It wore through on the day we hit the big seam, and nobody would let me throw it out after that.

exchanges.prompt: The crew you came up with?
reply: My first crew. Half of them still run that dig, and the other half taught them everything wrong.

beats._talk: Exchange 0 closes the talk and sets this beat's stage; the rest loop back in any order. Every prompt is askable cold off the greeting.

beats.journal: I have the drill bit. Now I need to take it to the crew at the <SecondPlace>.
beats.name: Drill Crate

beats.objective: Deliver the drill bit to the crew at the <SecondPlace>
beats.journal: I delivered the drill bit to the crew at the <SecondPlace>. They're putting it on the shelf above the shaft.

person.name: Arlo Breck
hellos: We're not hiring, if that's what you're after.

greeting: Is that the bit? She's sent it, then. We've not hit anything worth hauling in six weeks, and I'd stopped telling the crew it was the rock.

exchanges.prompt: She wants it back after a good month.
reply: She'll get it back. It's going on the shelf above the shaft, and you can tell her we didn't ask.

exchanges.prompt: Six dry weeks is hard on a crew's nerve.
reply: It is. They've been arguing about the shift rota for a week, and nobody argues about a rota when the rock's paying.

exchanges.prompt: You'd stopped telling them it was the rock?
reply: Because they'd stopped believing me. They'll believe the bit.

beats._talk: The HAND-BACK: the whole last step, so its stage is 100 and it takes the cargo. Prompts answer the greeting, or echo the first end's closing reply, which every player hears.
